subproblem.title: Uniform bound on Dφ for a C¹ map equal to the identity off a compact set
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, K ⊆ ℝ^P compact, and φ : ℝ^P → ℝ^P a C¹ map with φ(x) = x for every x ∉ K. Then there is Λ ∈ ℝ with Λ ≥ 0 and ‖Dφ(x)‖ ≤ Λ for every x ∈ ℝ^P, where Dφ(x) = fderiv ℝ φ x ∈ L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P) and ‖·‖ is the operator norm.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (K : Set (Euclid P)) (φ : Euclid P → Euclid P), IsCompact K → ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → (∀ x, x ∉ K → φ x = x) → ∃ Λ : ℝ, 0 ≤ Λ ∧ ∀ x, ‖fderiv ℝ φ x‖ ≤ Λ
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof. Simon 6.2.24(2)–(3) (chapter-06.txt lines 414–440) makes sense of f_#T for f "merely C¹ with f|spt T proper". The printed text omits this derivative estimate, so it is supplied here. Notation: E := ℝ^P (Euclid P); Dφ(x) := fderiv ℝ φ x ∈ E →L[ℝ] E; ‖·‖ is the operator norm.
1. Continuity of Dφ. φ is C¹, so x ↦ Dφ(x) is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv, using 1 ≠ 0).
2. Bound on K. K is compact and Dφ is continuous on K. So there is c ∈ ℝ with ‖Dφ(x)‖ ≤ c for all x ∈ K (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn).
3. Choice of Λ. Put Λ := max(1, c). Then 0 ≤ 1 ≤ Λ and c ≤ Λ.
4. Points of K. If x ∈ K, then ‖Dφ(x)‖ ≤ c ≤ Λ by steps 2–3.
5. Points off K. Let x ∉ K.
   - A compact subset of the Hausdorff space E is closed (IsCompact.isClosed), so E ∖ K is open and is a neighbourhood of x.
   - By hypothesis φ(y) = y for every y ∈ E ∖ K, so φ agrees with id on a neighbourhood of x (φ =ᶠ[𝓝 x] id).
   - The derivative at x depends only on the germ at x (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq). Hence Dφ(x) = D(id)(x) = id_E (fderiv_id).
   - Therefore ‖Dφ(x)‖ = ‖id_E‖ ≤ 1 ≤ Λ (ContinuousLinearMap.norm_id_le, step 3).
6. Conclusion. By steps 4–5, ‖Dφ(x)‖ ≤ Λ for every x ∈ E, and Λ ≥ 0 by step 3. So Λ is the required constant.
proof_key_steps: Dφ is continuous because φ is C¹.
Compactness of K gives c with ‖Dφ(x)‖ ≤ c on K.
K is closed, so φ = id near any x ∉ K; hence Dφ(x) = id and ‖Dφ(x)‖ ≤ 1.
Λ := max(1, c) ≥ 0 bounds ‖Dφ(x)‖ for every x.

audit.reason: The one-line proposition exactly matches the prose and includes every hypothesis. Continuity bounds the derivative on K; closedness makes φ locally identical to id outside K, giving derivative norm at most 1. Taking max(1,c) proves the stated global nonnegative bound, including P = 0. No circular reliance.

subproblem.title: IMRep orientations are a.e. unit: |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n). Then for Hⁿ⌞M-almost every x (i.e. μHE[n].restrict R.carrier-a.e.), every n-covector β ∈ Covector(ℝ^P, n) satisfies |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖, where ‖β‖ is the operator norm of β as a continuous alternating map.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict R.carrier), ∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) n, |R.orient x β| ≤ ‖β‖
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof; Simon 6.3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 735–746). There, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x) = τ₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τ_n for an orthonormal basis τ₁, …, τ_n of the approximate tangent space. The contract encodes this as IsUnitOrientationOf: ⟨α, ξ⟩ = ±α(τ₁, …, τ_n). Notation: μ := μHE[n].restrict R.carrier and ξ := R.orient. For an n-covector β (a continuous alternating map (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ), ‖β‖ is its operator norm.
1. Reduction to a pointwise claim. By the field R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there is a subspace Q of ℝ^P with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n R.carrier x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q. The a.e. filter is upward closed (filter_upwards). So it suffices to prove: if IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q holds for some Q, then |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ for every n-covector β.
2. Unfolding the orientation. IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q provides an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P (its span is Q, which is not needed) such that either
   (a) ξ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all n-covectors α, or
   (b) ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all n-covectors α.
3. Operator-norm bound at τ. Let β be an n-covector.
   - The operator-norm inequality for continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm) gives ‖β(τ)‖ ≤ ‖β‖ · ∏_{i<n} ‖τ_i‖.
   - Orthonormality gives ‖τ_i‖ = 1 for every i, so the product is 1. For n = 0 it is the empty product, also 1.
   - Since β(τ) is real, ‖β(τ)‖ = |β(τ)|. Hence |β(τ)| ≤ ‖β‖.
4. Both signs. In case (a), |ξ(x)(β)| = |β(τ)| ≤ ‖β‖. In case (b), |ξ(x)(β)| = |−β(τ)| = |β(τ)| ≤ ‖β‖ (abs_neg).
5. Conclusion. For μ-a.e. x, every n-covector β satisfies |R.orient x β| ≤ ‖β‖, which is the claim.
proof_key_steps: R.orients gives, μ-a.e., ξ(x) = ±(evaluation at an orthonormal τ).
Both signs give |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖; conclude by filter_upwards.

audit.reason: R.orients supplies a single almost-everywhere set on which the orientation formula holds for every covector. The alternating-map operator-norm inequality and orthonormality give the bound for either sign, including the empty product when n = 0. The prose, measure restriction and quantifier order exactly match the independent Lean proposition.

subproblem.title: Test-form convergence to 0 gives uniform smallness with a common compact support
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P and (ω_j)_{j∈ℕ} a sequence in 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n) with TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0. Then there is a compact C ⊆ U such that ω_j(x) = 0 for every j and every x ∉ C. Moreover, for every ε > 0, for all sufficiently large j, ‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ ε for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (ωs : ℕ → TestFormOn U n), TestFormOnConverges ωs 0 → ∃ C : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact C ∧ C ⊆ U ∧ (∀ j x, x ∉ C → (ωs j : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x = 0) ∧ ∀ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε → ∀ᶠ j in atTop, ∀ x, ‖(ωs j : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x‖ ≤ ε
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the first half of step 6 of the parent proof; Simon §6.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 170–176). There, ω_k → ω in 𝒟ⁿ(U) means spt ω_k ⊆ K for a fixed compact K ⊆ U and D^β ω_k → D^β ω uniformly on K. Here this is used with β = 0, as encoded by TestFormOnConverges. Notation: ω_j(x) := (ωs j : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x.
1. Unfolding. By definition of TestFormOnConverges ωs 0, there is C ⊆ ℝ^P such that:
   - C is compact and C ⊆ U;
   - tsupport ω_j ⊆ C for every j (and tsupport 0 ⊆ C, which is not needed);
   - for every k ∈ ℕ, iteratedFDeriv ℝ k ω_j → iteratedFDeriv ℝ k 0 uniformly on C as j → ∞.
   Take this C.
2. Vanishing off C. Let x ∉ C and j ∈ ℕ. Since tsupport ω_j ⊆ C, x ∉ tsupport ω_j, so ω_j(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). This is the third conjunct.
3. The case k = 0. The zero test form coerces to the zero form, so iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0 x = 0 for every x. Let ε > 0.
   - Uniform convergence for k = 0 (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff) gives j₀ such that for all j ≥ j₀ and x ∈ C, dist(iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0 x, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j x) < ε, i.e. ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j x‖ < ε.
   - Since ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 f x‖ = ‖f(x)‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero), this gives ‖ω_j(x)‖ < ε, hence ‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ ε, for x ∈ C.
4. Points off C. For j ≥ j₀ and x ∉ C, step 2 gives ‖ω_j(x)‖ = 0 ≤ ε.
5. Conclusion. For every ε > 0 and all sufficiently large j (∀ᶠ j in atTop), ‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ ε for all x ∈ ℝ^P. Together with steps 1–2, C satisfies all four conjuncts.
proof_key_steps: Unfold TestFormOnConverges: compact C ⊆ U contains every tsupport ω_j, and all iterated derivatives converge uniformly on C.
k = 0 and ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 f x‖ = ‖f x‖ give, eventually, ‖ω_j‖ < ε on C.
Combine: eventually ‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ ε for all x.

audit.reason: Unfolding the pinned convergence definition supplies precisely the required compact subset of U and common support. Zeroth-derivative uniform convergence gives eventual smallness on that set; vanishing outside it extends the bound globally. The proof establishes the exact eventual quantifiers and every conjunct of the one-line Lean proposition without another planning step.

subproblem.title: Integrability and sup-norm estimate for the IMRep pairing with a bounded, compactly supported covector field
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, R = (M, θ, ξ) an IMRep U n, C ⊆ U compact and B ∈ ℝ. Let F : ℝ^P → Covector(ℝ^P, n) be a.e. strongly measurable for μ := Hⁿ⌞M (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier), with F(x) = 0 for all x ∉ C and ‖F(x)‖ ≤ B for all x. Then x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(F(x)) is μ-integrable, and |∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(F(x)) dHⁿ(x)| ≤ B · (∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dHⁿ).toReal.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U C : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (F : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n) (B : ℝ), IsCompact C → C ⊆ U → AEStronglyMeasurable F (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier) → (∀ x, x ∉ C → F x = 0) → (∀ x, ‖F x‖ ≤ B) → Integrable (fun x => (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x (F x)) (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier) ∧ |∫ x in R.carrier, (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x (F x) ∂μHE[n]| ≤ B * (∫⁻ x in R.carrier ∩ C, (R.mult x : ℝ≥0∞) ∂μHE[n]).toReal
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2 and 4 of the parent proof, together with the estimate in its step 6. Simon 6.2.24(2) (chapter-06.txt lines 414–425) says that when M_W(T) < ∞ for W ⊂⊂ U, f_#T(ω) = ∫⟨ω(f(x)), df_x#ξ(x)⟩θ dHⁿ makes sense for C¹ f. The printed text leaves the integrability and the estimate to the reader; they are supplied here. This proof uses the sibling theorem orient_bound (Submission.dpf_pfc_imrep_orient_abs_apply_le).
Notation:
- M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient, μ := μHE[n].restrict M;
- h(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(F(x)), with θ(x) viewed in ℝ;
- 1_C θ := C.indicator (fun y => (θ y : ℝ)) and g(x) := B·(1_C θ)(x).
1. C is measurable. C is compact, hence closed (IsCompact.isClosed), hence a Borel, i.e. measurable, set.
2. θ is measurable. θ : ℝ^P → ℕ is measurable (R.measurable_mult), and every function on ℕ is measurable (measurable_from_nat). So x ↦ (θ(x) : ℝ) is measurable, hence a.e. strongly measurable.
3. Restriction identity. Since C is measurable, μ.restrict C = (μHE[n].restrict M).restrict C = μHE[n].restrict (C ∩ M) = μHE[n].restrict (M ∩ C) (Measure.restrict_restrict, inter_comm).
4. 1_C θ and g are μ-integrable.
   - By R.locallyIntegrable_mult applied to the compact set C ⊆ U, ∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dμHE[n] ≠ ∞.
   - Since θ(x) ≥ 0, its extended norm ‖(θ(x) : ℝ)‖ₑ equals (θ(x) : ℝ≥0∞) (Real.enorm_natCast). By step 3, ∫⁻ ‖θ‖ₑ d(μ.restrict C) = ∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dμHE[n] < ∞.
   - With step 2, θ is integrable on C with respect to μ (IntegrableOn).
   - Hence 1_C θ is μ-integrable (integrable_indicator_iff, C measurable), and so is g = B·1_C θ (Integrable.const_mul).
5. h is μ-a.e. strongly measurable.
   - The evaluation map (ζ, β) ↦ ζ(β) from MultiVector P n × Covector (Euclid P) n to ℝ is continuous, since ζ ranges over continuous linear maps (continuous_fst.clm_apply continuous_snd).
   - ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient), and so is F (hypothesis). So x ↦ ξ(x)(F(x)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂).
   - Multiplying by the measurable θ of step 2 preserves this (AEStronglyMeasurable.mul).
6. Domination |h| ≤ g μ-a.e. By orient_bound, for μ-a.e. x, |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ for all n-covectors β. Fix such an x.
   - If x ∈ C, then (1_C θ)(x) = θ(x). Using θ(x) ≥ 0 and ‖F(x)‖ ≤ B: |h(x)| = θ(x)·|ξ(x)(F(x))| ≤ θ(x)·‖F(x)‖ ≤ θ(x)·B = g(x).
   - If x ∉ C, then F(x) = 0 by hypothesis, so ξ(x)(F(x)) = 0 (ξ(x) is linear) and |h(x)| = 0. Also g(x) = B·0 = 0.
   Hence ‖h(x)‖ ≤ g(x) for μ-a.e. x.
7. Integrability. h is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (step 5) and dominated μ-a.e. by the μ-integrable g (steps 4 and 6). So h is μ-integrable (Integrable.mono'). This is the first conjunct.
8. Value of ∫ g dμ:
   ∫ g dμ = B·∫ 1_C θ dμ (integral_const_mul)
   = B·∫ θ d(μ.restrict C) (integral_indicator, C measurable)
   = B·∫ θ d(μHE[n].restrict (M ∩ C)) (step 3)
   = B·(∫⁻_{M∩C} ENNReal.ofReal(θ) dμHE[n]).toReal (integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae; θ ≥ 0 and is a.e. strongly measurable)
   = B·(∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dμHE[n]).toReal (ENNReal.ofReal_natCast).
9. Estimate. By definition of the set integral, ∫_M θ ξ(F) dμHE[n] = ∫ h dμ. Then |∫ h dμ| = ‖∫ h dμ‖ ≤ ∫ g dμ (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le, using integrability of g and step 6). By step 8 this gives |∫_M θ ξ(F) dμHE[n]| ≤ B·(∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dμHE[n]).toReal, the second conjunct.
proof_key_steps: C compact ⇒ measurable; θ measurable; μ.restrict C = Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ C).
Local integrability of θ on the compact C ⊆ U makes g = B·1_C θ μ-integrable.
h = θ·ξ(F) is a.e. strongly measurable via continuity of evaluation.
orient_bound together with F = 0 off C and ‖F‖ ≤ B gives |h| ≤ g μ-a.e.
Integrable.mono' gives integrability; |∫ h| ≤ ∫ g = B·(∫⁻_{M∩C} θ).toReal.

audit.reason: The proof establishes measurability, the correct restriction identity, integrability of the multiplicity indicator, and almost-everywhere domination using only the declared orient_bound dependency. Integrating the majorant gives exactly the stated ENNReal.toReal bound. No additional B ≥ 0 hypothesis is needed: the global norm bound implies it. Both conjuncts match the prose and are proved without gaps or circularity.
